question.problem: Find the curvature of the curve $y=2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-1)$ at $x=2.$
question.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ(x)$ of a plane curve $y=y(x)$ is given by

$$
κ(x)=\frac{|{y}^{″}(x)|}{(1+[{y}^{′}(x)]^{2})^{3/2}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${y}^{′}(x)$ and ${y}^{″}(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & =\frac{2}{x-1},\, & {y}^{″}(x) & =-\frac{2}{(x-1)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these into the formula for the curvature, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(x) & =\frac{|-\frac{2}{(x-1)^{2}}|}{{[1+{(\frac{2}{x-1})}^{2}]}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{(x-1)^{2}{[1+\frac{4}{(x-1)^{2}}]}^{3/2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the curvature at $x=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(2) & =\frac{2}{(2-1)^{2}{[1+\frac{4}{(2-1)^{2}}]}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{{5}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$
